title: Experts, Errors, and Context: A Large-Scale Study of Human Evaluation for Machine Translation
primary_evidence: TACL 2021 study uses professional MQM raters, full document context, anonymized systems and randomized presentation. Expert-derived rankings differ from crowd rankings. Full paper inspected.
proposed_use: Adapt error-span annotation, reviewer calibration and blinded paired evaluation to Pahlavi.
limitations: English-German and Chinese-English evidence; no Pahlavi validation. Expert agreement is imperfect. Reported study, not independently replicated here.

title: Evaluating LLM-Based Translation of a Low-Resource Technical Language: The Medical and Philosophical Greek of Galen
institution: Vanderbilt University; Harvard University Center for Hellenic Studies and Classics; Australian National University MINT Lab; independent researcher
primary_evidence: April 2026 preprint revision: 60 blinded translations of 20 paragraphs from two Galenic works; expert modified MQM and seven automatic metrics. Rare technical passages concentrate catastrophic errors. Full paper inspected.
proposed_use: Stratify Pahlavi tests by terminology rarity and genre; record serious semantic errors separately from mean quality.
limitations: Two works and small sample; rarity correlation strongly influenced by two passages. Ancient Greek is not Pahlavi; no independent replication here.

title: MITRA-zh-eval: Using a Buddhist Chinese Language Evaluation Dataset to Assess Machine Translation and Evaluation Metrics
institution: University of California Berkeley BAIR; Temple University; Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf
primary_evidence: 2025 paper compares metrics against 182 outputs rated by five subject specialists; average pairwise rater Spearman correlation 0.4. GEMBA performs best in their calibration. Human calibration excludes the judge model's outputs.
proposed_use: Calibrate any automated Pahlavi judge against qualified independent judgments before using it for selection.
limitations: Authors report no specific annotator training; modest agreement and beginning-of-text sampling. This supports conditional judge usefulness, not universal validity. No replication here.

title: COMET for Low-Resource Machine Translation Evaluation: A Case Study of English-Maltese and Spanish-Basque
institution: University of Malta; HiTZ Center, University of the Basque Country
primary_evidence: LREC-COLING2024 paper tests unsupported or weakly supported language settings against human judgments; metric fine-tuning can help, but sensitivity to training-score distributions and inconsistent gains remain.
proposed_use: Treat Pahlavi COMET as an uncalibrated diagnostic until rank and serious-error detection are measured.
limitations: Case studies do not establish Pahlavi behavior. Encoder language coverage differs from quality-estimation training coverage. Full paper inspected; not replicated.

title: COMET official documentation: Languages Covered and Interpreting Scores
primary_evidence: Official README explicitly warns that uncovered language pairs produce unreliable results. Its listed XLM-R language coverage includes Persian, but not Pahlavi/Middle Persian. Model-specific scoring and comparison interfaces are documented.
proposed_use: Record metric checkpoint/version and coverage; never interpret a high unvalidated score as a percentage of correct Pahlavi meaning.
limitations: README inspection only; no metric inference or source-code execution. Persian support cannot be equated with historical Middle Persian support.

title: On Compositional Generalization of Neural Machine Translation; CoGnition
institution: Zhejiang University; Westlake University; Westlake Institute for Advanced Study
primary_evidence: ACL2021 benchmark separately tests novel compounds and ordinary test sentences; standard translation scores can hide compound errors. Public repository README supplies dataset splits and evaluation entry point at github.com/yafuly/CoGnition.
proposed_use: Create expert-validated Pahlavi novel-combination families and score the changed proposition directly.
limitations: English-Chinese construction, not a Pahlavi test. Repository README inspected; evaluation Python source retrieval failed and no code ran.

title: Measuring Compositional Generalization: A Comprehensive Method on Realistic Data
primary_evidence: ICLR2020 DBCA constructs partitions with similar distributions of atomic elements but different compound distributions. Demonstrated on CFQ semantic parsing/question answering.
proposed_use: Separate vocabulary unfamiliarity from unfamiliar combinations; document atom and combination exposure in diagnostic splits.
limitations: CFQ is not ordinary translation. Pahlavi atoms and grammatical compounds need defensible annotation; arbitrary string swaps do not implement DBCA.

title: Evaluation and Large-scale Training for Contextual Machine Translation
primary_evidence: WMT2024 compares contextual training/inference and tests both contrastive scoring and actual generation. Contrastive preference is only a proxy for generating the contextually correct form; context-dense evaluation reveals otherwise small gains.
proposed_use: Evaluate real translated outputs under correct, removed and misleading context, including referents and ellipsis.
limitations: Modern language pairs; no Pahlavi result. Generated neighboring translations and gold target context are distinct conditions. Paper inspected; no execution.

title: When Flores Bloomz Wrong: Cross-Direction Contamination in Machine Translation Evaluation
institution: Saarland University; Queen's University Belfast; DFKI; University of Edinburgh
primary_evidence: EACL2026 study demonstrates target-side memorization can inflate other translation directions; source paraphrasing and entity changes do not reliably remove memorized-reference effects.
proposed_use: Group all directions, translations and derived samples by passage/work lineage before partitioning; probe memorization separately.
limitations: Bloomz/FLORES case study is not proof a particular Pahlavi model is contaminated. Foundation-model corpus exposure cannot be fully certified here.

title: When LLMs Struggle: Reference-less Translation Evaluation for Low-resource Languages
institution: University of Surrey Institute for People-Centred AI and Centre for Translation Studies
primary_evidence: LoResLM2025 tests prompting and instruction-tuning for quality estimation; prompt-based LLM approaches are outperformed by fine-tuned encoder-based QE, with transliteration and named-entity failures.
proposed_use: Test judges on controlled semantic corruptions and correct paraphrases, independently of translator selection.
limitations: Studied modern low-resource directions and contemporary checkpoints; not proof all future LLM judges fail. No Pahlavi judge validation or replication here.

title: Statistical Power and Translationese in Machine Translation Evaluation
institution: Trinity College Dublin ADAPT; University of Edinburgh; Johns Hopkins University
primary_evidence: EMNLP2020 shows source-original versus reverse-created test material can change conclusions and cautions that low-powered nonsignificant comparisons do not establish human parity.
proposed_use: Mark original composition language; distinguish translating natural English/Farsi into Pahlavi from reconstructing a Pahlavi original from its scholarly translation. Plan precision before acceptance.
limitations: Do not infer a universal sample size. Reverse pairs can be useful training and reconstruction tests, but represent a different evaluation population.

title: Statistical Significance Tests for Machine Translation Evaluation
institution: MIT Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory
primary_evidence: EMNLP2004 primary paper describes paired bootstrap comparisons and tests their behavior for BLEU. Provides a foundational uncertainty method for comparing systems on shared examples.
proposed_use: Compare candidates on identical items; extend resampling to independent work/passage-family clusters for this project.
limitations: Cluster resampling is our design extension, not a claim that this paper validated Pahlavi human scores. Small numbers of independent works still limit inference.
